chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Jabala, from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person in ihram who is shaded while he is in ihram. He said: 'There is no harm, except for the sick or the one who has an ailment, and the one who cannot endure the sun.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in ihram to be shaded from the sun?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the general prohibition against a muhrim seeking shade is nuanced to highlight the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship). The Imam specifies that shading is not only permissible but necessary for those suffering from illness or unable to endure the sun's heat, illustrating the flexibility of fiqh in accommodating physical weakness during the sacred state of ihram.
